A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Go-Browse research. Their text, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset collection, WebArena evaluations, and analyses of task diversity, navigation depth, and prefixed sampling.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Online-Mind2Web evaluation, component analyses, collection-cost analysis, and bootstrap significance tests.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3, the exploration frontier, NavExplorer and PageExplorer, feasibility filtering, prefixed/unprefixed sampling, and supervised fine-tuning remain unchanged. The new component analyses examine existing procedures rather than introduce method changes.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only within the five WebArena domains. v2 adds Online-Mind2Web evaluation covering 300 tasks across 136 live websites, substantially extending evaluation to unfamiliar environments. The WebArena training dataset is retained.

E2.justification: The WebArena comparator membership is identical in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3. The added Online-Mind2Web comparison reuses NNetNav-7B and GPT-4o-mini; newly cited concurrent methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing WebArena collection, fine-tuning, and evaluation settings are retained. New analysis designs include holding proposed tasks at 30 per domain while varying resets across 1, 5, and 15, and stratifying Online-Mind2Web results using GPT-4o-mini domain-adjacency classifications and benchmark difficulty labels.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained diversity, depth, and prefixed-sampling analyses, v2 adds an outer-loop coverage ablation, feasibility-filter efficiency analysis, task-proposer and explorer-type comparisons, and Online-Mind2Web domain/difficulty breakdowns with success/failure examples. These substantially expand investigation of component behavior and generalization.

E5.justification: v1 provides no formal uncertainty or significance analysis. v2 Appendix B.3 introduces 10,000-sample paired bootstrap tests with win/tie ratios and p-values for the WebArena comparisons, including p = 0.094 against NNetNav and p = 0.108 against GPT-4o-mini. These are benchmark-result resamples, not reported additional training runs.

E6.justification: Existing WebArena scores are unchanged. New results include Online-Mind2Web success rates of 5.33%, 4.00%, and 9.33% for Go-Browse, NNetNav, and GPT-4o-mini, respectively; coverage of 183, 214, and 260 URLs under different reset settings; and task-proposal and cost measurements. However, Figure 8 totals 13 Go-Browse successes, whereas Table 2 implies 16 of 300; no different subset is explained.

T1.justification: The state/action, trajectory, binary-reward, and URL-graph formulations are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the structured-exploration contribution, dataset release, and headline 21.7% WebArena result, including the 2.9-point advantage over NNetNav and 2.4-point advantage over GPT-4o-mini. Added experiments do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting Claude's proposal efficiency and GPT-4o's task diversity to their complementary roles, and interprets the new coverage and filtering analyses. Appendix B.4 qualifies generalization: Go-Browse's advantage is concentrated on WebArena-adjacent websites, while NNetNav performs better on truly out-of-domain tasks, mainly through easier tasks. A new limitation addresses propagation of model and prompt biases.

D1.justification: v2 adds model-level collection-cost details, cached-token and pricing assumptions, and the NNetNav-WA Apache 2.0 license. Existing prompts, action space, hardware, training time, hyperparameters, and release URL are retained; the original hyperparameter appendix moves from B to C.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds concurrent methods Explorer, OS-Genesis, and InSTA, distinguishing Go-Browse through explicit construction and use of its web graph. v2 also adds Online-Mind2Web and pricing references and changes reward-model attribution from AutoEval to Pan et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose corrections and compression, replaces numbered background/method subsections with titled paragraphs, and changes citation and terminology styling. It adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements and reorganizes the appendices, while preserving the main narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables and two figures covering transfer results, coverage controls, proposer comparisons, costs, bootstrap tests, and task examples. Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated within the conference layout, including separation of the diversity and depth plots. This substantially expands the visual presentation beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves support and transparency for the unchanged method through controlled coverage analysis, bootstrap uncertainty reporting, collection-cost accounting, and evaluation beyond WebArena. However, the new generalization evidence is not fully reconciled: Table 2 implies 16 Go-Browse successes, while Figure 8 shows 13 without explaining a subset. The additions provide a useful net improvement, but this reporting gap limits confidence in an important extension.
